commitResults.messageTitle: Add help command listing every command
commitResults.messageBody:
New users have no way to discover the available commands without
reading the user guide (user story #7, feature F6.1).

Add a HelpCommand class that holds the format and one example of
every command, grouped by feature as in the user guide. Keep the text
in its own class so StudentCommands only gains a single case line,
which reduces merge conflicts with teammates adding commands there.

Words typed after help are ignored, as the user guide specifies.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add storage: auto-save, save and reload commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Records were kept only in memory, so everything was lost on exit
(US42), and tutors could not fix records outside the app (US43).

Save all records to data/tutorledger.txt, a plain-text file with one
record per line, after every command that changes data, and load it
on startup. Add save [FILE_PATH] to confirm a save or write a backup
copy, and reload to read the file again after editing it by hand.

Changes are detected by comparing the saved form of the data before
and after each command. Commands added later are therefore saved
without extra code, and display-only commands never overwrite hand
edits. reload does not save, so lines it skips are not erased before
they can be fixed.

A bad line in the file is skipped and reported with its line number
instead of crashing. Records are rebuilt through the same validation
as typed commands. The ID counters are saved so deleted IDs are never
reused.

The lesson commands take prefixed values such as d/, t/ and note/,
which are read exactly the way the student commands read n/, l/ and
p/. The parser for these is private to StudentCommands, so the lesson
commands cannot use it without copying it.

Move parseFields and the Fields record into a package-private
ArgumentParser class, so that both command groups share one
implementation and a prefix is always read the same way.

The moved code is unchanged, so StudentCommands behaves as before.
Add ArgumentParserTest to cover the parser directly.

Lesson is immutable, and the only change it supports is
withPaymentStatus. Recording a lesson's outcome (F2.3) and editing a
lesson (F2.4) both need a copy with other details changed.

Add withDetails, which takes the new subject, date, time, attendance,
fee and notes, and treats null as "keep the current value". The ID,
student and payment status are always carried over unchanged.

Use one method with nullable arguments rather than a withX method per
field, because an edit can change any combination of fields at once
and the caller would otherwise chain up to six copies.

Add isRecorded so that callers can ask whether attendance has been
taken without comparing against the enum themselves.

TutorLedgerData can only store a lesson that already has an ID
(putLesson). That is enough for the student and payment tests, but
the lesson commands need to create, change and remove lessons.

Add the operations those commands need:

* addLesson assigns the next L<number> ID and stores a lesson that
  starts as not recorded and unpaid. The counter never decreases, so
  an ID is never reused after a deletion, as with students and
  homework.
* replaceLesson swaps in a changed copy of an existing lesson.
* deleteLesson removes one lesson and returns it for reporting.

Enforce in addLesson and replaceLesson the user guide rule that two
lessons cannot start at the same date and time. The rule applies
across students because there is a single tutor. replaceLesson checks
only a lesson that actually moved, so that changing a fee or a note
is never blocked by it.

Leave putLesson without the check so that it keeps accepting any
lesson, as the existing tests and a future data file reload expect.
Let it advance the ID counter the same way putHomework does.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add schedule command to create a lesson
commitResults.messageBody:
A tutor needs one place that holds the whole teaching schedule (user
story #10), but there is no way to create a lesson from the command
line: lessons can only be put into TutorLedgerData by tests.

Add LessonCommands with the schedule command (F2.1):

    schedule STUDENT_ID d/DATE t/TIME s/SUBJECT f/FEE

Give LessonCommands the same shape as HomeworkCommands and
PaymentCommands, so the main loop treats every command group alike:
a static handles() routes input to it, and execute() returns the text
to print, with validation problems reported as an "Error: ..." line.

Apply the rules from the user guide:

* SUBJECT must be one of the student's subjects. The match ignores
  case and the lesson stores the student's own spelling, so that
  "a math" and "A Math" do not become two different subjects.
* Two lessons cannot start at the same date and time.
* A new lesson starts as not recorded and unpaid.

Route schedule to LessonCommands in the main loop.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add lessons command to list upcoming lessons
commitResults.messageBody:
Before a teaching day the tutor wants to know who is next and when
(user story #14). Scheduled lessons can only be seen one student at a
time, through view.

Add the lessons command (F2.2):

    lessons [week]

List today's lessons when no argument is given, and the lessons from
Monday to Sunday of the current week when "week" is given. Sort by
date and then start time, so that the list reads in the order the
lessons happen regardless of the order they were scheduled in. Pad
the ID and student columns so that the rows line up.

Reject any other argument with the command's format instead of
ignoring it, because the user guide lets only owed, reload and help
ignore extra words.

Take today's date from the injected Clock, so that the tests can pin
it to a known Monday.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add record command for lesson outcomes
commitResults.messageBody:
After a lesson the tutor wants to note whether the student came and
what was covered, so that the next lesson can pick up from there
(user stories #21, #22 and #16). Nothing can set a lesson's
attendance or notes, so every lesson stays "not recorded".

Add the record command (F2.3):

    record LESSON_ID a/ATTENDANCE [note/NOTES]

Apply the rules from the user guide:

* Only a lesson dated today or earlier can be recorded, since a
  lesson that has not happened has no outcome yet.
* Recording again replaces the attendance, and replaces the notes
  only if note/ is given. A bare note/ clears them.
* ATTENDANCE must be present, absent or late. Reject "not recorded"
  even though the Lesson model can hold it, because it is the state a
  lesson starts in rather than an outcome.

Build the recorded lesson with Lesson.withDetails, so that its
subject, slot, fee and payment status are carried over untouched.

A lesson that is moved, mispriced or recorded wrongly can only be
fixed by deleting it and entering it again (user story #36).

Add lesson editing (F2.4):

    edit LESSON_ID [d/DATE] [t/TIME] [s/SUBJECT] [f/FEE]
                   [a/ATTENDANCE] [note/NOTES]

edit is the command word students already use. Follow the user guide
and let the first letter of the ID decide which kind of item is
meant: LessonCommands.handles() claims edit only when the ID starts
with L, and StudentCommands keeps every other case. This keeps the
command list short, at the cost of one shared word. A value such as
l/Sec 4 is not mistaken for a lesson ID.

Keep the values that are left out, and apply the rules of schedule
and record to the new ones:

* SUBJECT must be one of the student's subjects.
* The lesson cannot move onto another lesson's date and time.
* A lesson dated after today cannot hold attendance or notes. This
  also stops a recorded lesson being moved into the future, which
  would leave it in a state that record can never produce.

Validate the whole edit before storing anything, so that one bad
value never leaves a lesson half changed. Leave payment status to
mark, which already owns it.

A lesson scheduled by mistake stays in the schedule and is counted
in what the student owes, because there is no way to remove a single
lesson (user story #37). The only removal is deleting the whole
student.

Add lesson deletion (F2.5):

    delete LESSON_ID

Share the delete command word with students the same way edit is
shared: the first letter of the ID decides which kind of item is
meant, so "delete L44" removes a lesson and "delete S5" still removes
a student.

Remove only the lesson. The student and their homework are left
alone, and the lesson's ID is not reused.

commitResults.messageTitle: User Guide: Document all v1.0 commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide still holds the template's todo example and documents
only save and reload, so the published guide does not tell tutors how
to use the student, lesson, homework, payment, help or exit commands
that v1.0 ships.

Fill in the guide from the v1.0 draft in the user stories document,
corrected against the current code:

- Add an introduction, quick start, command format notes and a table
  of accepted values, IDs and prefixes.
- Add a section for every command, with example output captured from
  one real session so that IDs and totals agree across sections.
- Describe actual behaviour where it differs from the draft, e.g.
  owed rejects extra words, notes cannot contain "word/", and a
  skipped student line also skips that student's lessons and homework.
- Add known issues, an extra FAQ entry and a full command summary.
- Use Java 25, as the build requires, instead of the draft's Java 17.

commitResults.messageTitle: build.gradle: Enable assertions for the run task
commitResults.messageBody:
Java ignores assert statements unless the JVM is started with -ea, so
the assertions being added to the code would never be checked when the
app is launched with gradlew run. The test task already enables them
by default.

Set enableAssertions on the run task so that assertions are checked
during manual testing as well as during unit tests.

The lesson commands leave no trace of which command ran, what it did,
or why it was rejected, which makes a misbehaving command hard to
diagnose after the fact.

Log each lesson command, its outcome and any rejection. Use FINE so
the trace appears only when debug logging is enabled and never
clutters the tutor's screen, matching the rejected-command logging
already in StudentCommands.

Assert the assumptions the commands rely on, such as the delete branch
being the only command word left after the earlier cases, a newly
scheduled lesson having no attendance, and a recorded lesson having
attendance. These catch programming mistakes, while invalid user input
is still reported through the existing error messages.

commitResults.messageTitle: Lesson data: Assert lesson and parser invariants
commitResults.messageBody:
The lesson model, lesson storage and argument parser rely on
assumptions that nothing checks. For example, the validated Lesson
constructor trusts its caller completely, and addLesson relies on
putLesson advancing the lesson counter so the next lesson does not
overwrite this one.

Assert these preconditions and postconditions so that a programming
mistake fails fast at its source instead of silently corrupting a
lesson record:
* Lesson: the unvalidated constructor receives valid values, and
  withDetails keeps the lesson ID, student and payment status.
* TutorLedgerData: adding advances the counter and stores the lesson,
  replacing keeps the student, and deleting removes the lesson.
* ArgumentParser: allowed prefixes are lower-case letters, and every
  prefix found has a value.

Also log the completion of lesson replacement and deletion at FINE.
